Subject: SLA amendment request — uptime floor & monthly remedy

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for a productive demo last week. BlueOak is moving quickly toward a procurement decision, but Legal asked us to propose two small changes to Redwood's standard SLA template before we sign:

1) Uptime floor: we need a temporary availability floor of 99.7% (Redwood standard is 99.9%) for the first 6 months post-cutover, given our heavy prefix-cached workloads during ramp.
2) Monthly remedy cushion: instead of per-incident credits, we want a monthly "cushion" that aggregates minor degradations and provides a single monthly remedy calculation (our internal procurement prefers predictable bookkeeping).

I've attached BlueOak_SLA_Amendment_0317.pdf with the requested redlines and a concise explanation of why this gives us the operational breathing room during ramp. Could you and your contracts lead confirm whether these are workable? If not, we can propose compromise language.

Also copying Claire (ops) and contracts for context.

Best,
Ethan

Ethan — thanks for the note and the clear redlines. We're keen to get BlueOak live and want to be pragmatic here. Quick responses to the two asks: 

1) Uptime floor
We typically hold to 99.9% for hosted customers. For a limited ramp period we can consider 99.7% if paired with explicit operational commitments: detailed cutover plan, weekly ramp check-ins for the first 30 days, and a rollback/fallback path if prefix cache warm-up exceeds thresholds.

2) Monthly remedy cushion
We prefer remedies tied to measured availability windows rather than an opaque monthly pool, but we're open to a hybrid: aggregate minor degradations into a monthly calculation with a per-month cap (to keep economic exposure bounded).

I'll loop Ben on the proposed cap and Marissa on the operational commitments. If you can sign off on a 6-month pilot timeline and share the cutover plan, we should be able to land this quickly.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to align on the pilot carveouts and remedy cap. What time works?

—Laura

Subject: FW: BlueOak SLA asks — proposed commercial guardrails (internal)

Laura/Marissa — forwarding Ethan's request. My read: accept the 99.7% temporary floor only if we set a simple monthly cap on credits and define maintenance carveouts precisely. My suggested commercial terms (for internal review before we counter):

- Pilot window: 6 months from production cutover.
- Uptime floor during pilot: 99.7%.
- Monthly remedy calculation: aggregate minutes of unavailability beyond the floor into a single monthly credit equal to X% of that month's invoice, where X = min(10%, computed_remedy).
- Per-incident hard cap: no single incident can trigger more than 50% of that month's remedy cap.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance with 48h notice and emergency maintenance with post-facto notification up to 4 hours are excluded, provided incidents are logged in our dashboard.

Marissa — can you confirm the operational asks: weekly ramp check-ins, metrics we'll publish, and what rollback triggers make sense? Also flag any engineering risks that would prevent offering a 6-month pilot.

- Ben
Senior Director, Commercial

Note: internal only — do not send until legal oks the cap wording.

Ethan — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. We've drafted a short compromise that we believe meets BlueOak's bookkeeping needs while protecting both parties. High level:

1) Pilot & uptime floor
- 6-month pilot starting at production cutover.
- During pilot Redwood will accept a temporary uptime floor of 99.7%.
- Weekly 30-minute ramp check-ins for first 30 days, then biweekly reviews for remainder of pilot.

2) Monthly remedy cushion (compromise model)
- All availability shortfalls below the uptime floor in a given month will be aggregated into a single monthly remedy amount.
- Remedy = min(10% of that month's Redwood invoice, computed_remedy_based_on_minutes_below_floor).
- No single incident can consume more than 50% of the monthly remedy cap.

3) Maintenance & carveouts
- Scheduled maintenance (48h notice) and emergency maintenance (post-facto notification within 4h) are carveouts provided incidents are recorded.

4) Review clause
- Parties will review pilot metrics at month 5 to decide on returning to standard 99.9% or extending the amended floor.

If BlueOak is comfortable, we can convert this into tracked redlines and route to DocuSign. I've attached the draft amendment and a DocuSign link to expedite. If you prefer a short call to sign off, happy to schedule.

Regards,
Laura
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
